newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tougher S.African financial control needed.
newsitem.headline: Tougher S.African financial control needed.

text.p: South African Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Tuesday a major review was urgently needed of the supervision and regulation of financial services to improve consumer protection.

Introducing the Financial Institutions Amendment Bill in parliament, Marcus said the present system of regulating and supervising the financial services sector was fragmented and did not take into account the fact that prudential regulation was not static.
"In a changing environment such as ours, the various dimensions of prudential regulation requires regular upgrading and attention," she said.
"But prudential regulation is meaningless unless complied with. In particular, prudential supervision must, by its very nature, be both intrusive and compliance-based."

This required the regulator to be given appropriate powers and resources to act. The bill aimed at meeting some of these concerns, albeit in a limited way. At least another 21 bills were being prepared to address other areas.
"There is much debate about a complaints-driven approach or one driven by compliance with a set of rules," she said.
"In looking at a complaints-driven approach, the role of an industry compensation scheme for victimised investors needs consideration.
"In my view, we need to find an approach that is manageable, enforceable and effective in our very diverse industry."

Penalties for abuse and non-compliance also had to be signifcant, and could range from public reprimands, personal or corporate fines, the confiscation of illicit profits and even banning from the industry.

"We need to ensure that the principals of firms, whether product suppliers or marketing firms, are held accountable for the actions of their employees, thereby ensuring management attention to effective control, recruitment and training," she said.
"This is linked to the need for full disclosure with regard to the product being sold, commissions paid and the ultimate benefit the consumer will receive."
This called for an extensive education campaign by the industry as well as government.
